summary: The The X Finders project (AstroBlink-IR / TNO-PlanetX-Detector) focuses on the scientific identification and detection of potential Trans-Neptunian Objects (TNOs) and Planet X candidates using advanced infrared data processing. By leveraging multi-epoch infrared observations and analyzing specific color indices—particularly utilizing the principle that typical stars cluster around W1 - W2 ≈ 0, whereas colder candidate objects exhibit distinct color signatures—the project effectively isolates moving celestial bodies against background stellar fields. The methodology combines automated data pipelines with rigorous spatial mapping across right ascension and declination coordinates. To ensure maximum accessibility and clarity for independent remote readers and evaluators, the presentation is structured around clean, self-explanatory visual charts and structured text blocks rather than complex interactive triggers. This guarantees that technical findings—such as 6-month epoch displacement vectors and differential astrometric offsets—are communicated with absolute professional transparency and scientific precision.
details:
The AstroBlink-IR / TNO-PlanetX-Detector project focuses on the scientific identification and detection of potential Trans-Neptunian Objects (TNOs) and Planet X candidates using advanced infrared data processing. By leveraging multi-epoch infrared observations and analyzing specific color indices—particularly utilizing the principle that typical stars cluster around W1 - W2 ≈ 0, whereas colder candidate objects exhibit distinct color signatures—the project effectively isolates moving celestial bodies against background stellar fields.

How It Works & Tools Used

The methodology combines automated data pipelines with rigorous spatial mapping across right ascension and declination coordinates. To achieve this, the project utilizes powerful programming tools and automated data processing frameworks (including Python and quantitative scripting) to fetch, clean, and process multi-epoch astronomical data, tracking differential astrometric offsets and 6-month epoch displacement vectors.

Impact, Innovation & Creativity

The intended impact is to provide a scalable, accessible, and rigorous computational framework that streamlines the search for outer-Solar-System bodies. The project creatively bridges large-scale astronomical datasets with automated detection pipelines, ensuring that technical findings are communicated with absolute professional transparency, clarity, and scientific precision for independent evaluators and researchers alike.
